svg.title: Theta Plotter Photo-Style Wiring Layout - No Overlaps
svg.desc: Photo-style wiring layout using peripheral terminal faces, 90-degree wiring, explicit distribution blocks, and no wire overlap across components or other wires.
svg.text: Theta Pen Plotter - Photo-Style Wiring Layout
No wires overlap other wires or pass across terminals. All wire paths use 90-degree segments in dedicated routing lanes.

g.text: 1. PSU terminal face to fused DIN distribution
Wires exit downward into empty routing lanes, then enter the distribution block. They do not pass over the PSU terminal strip.
Only one +V and one -V PSU output are shown feeding the fused distribution input. Use ferrules and strain relief; do not use +V ADJ as a power terminal.
2. Motion axis wiring pattern - repeat for X, Y, and A
This is one axis, routed as lanes. Substitute X/Y/A terminal groups and the matching fused branch.
Use X, Y, or A branch.
X: RP23CNC X terminal group, X G common, X fused branch, X TB6600, X motor.
Y and A use the same physical pattern with their matching terminal groups, fused branches, drivers, and motors.
Current toolhead MCU: SparkFun Pro Micro RP2350; verify remaining module and power endpoints against the master wiring table.
Preferred: HX711 near load cell; long harness carries power and digital/control lines.
Motion: RP23CNC axis G is intentionally commoned to TB6600 PUL-, DIR-, and ENA- through the axis G common block. Axis Stp/Dir/En go to TB6600 PUL+/DIR+/ENA+.
Stepper motor: TB6600 A+ -> black, A- -> green, B+ -> red, B- -> blue. Confirm coil pairs with an ohmmeter before power.
Power: MEISHILE +V/-V feeds the fused DIN distribution. Use separate fused branches for X/Y/A drivers and the toolhead buck inputs.
